facts.text: Neutron stars can spin at blinding speeds of up to 700 rotations per second, packing the mass of two Suns into a sphere the size of a city.
facts.claimText: Neutron stars can spin at speeds of up to 700 rotations per second while packing the mass of two Suns into a city-sized sphere.
facts.explanation: Millisecond pulsars are ultra-dense neutron stars whose rapid rotation is powered by angular momentum conservation and accretion.

facts.text: A full NASA extravehicular spacesuit costs approximately twelve million dollars, with over seventy percent of the budget dedicated to the backpack life-support unit.
facts.claimText: Over seventy percent of a twelve-million-dollar NASA spacesuit budget goes solely toward decorative solar-reflective gold visors.
facts.explanation: Myth! Over 70% of an extravehicular spacesuit cost goes to the Primary Life Support Subsystem backpack, not the visor.

facts.text: There is a hyper-dense diamond planet known as 55 Cancri e where intense interior pressure has crystallized carbon into celestial gemstones.
facts.claimText: Exoplanet 55 Cancri e has oceans of liquid diamond on its outer crust.
facts.explanation: While its mantle is theorized to be rich in crystalline diamond and graphite, its surface is molten lava rather than liquid diamond.

facts.text: Footprints left by Apollo astronauts on the Moon could remain undisturbed for at least one hundred million years because there is no wind or liquid erosion.
facts.claimText: Apollo astronaut footprints on the Moon can last for at least 100 million years because the Moon lacks wind and liquid water erosion.
facts.explanation: Without an atmosphere, wind, or rain, lunar surface regolith is only disturbed over eons by microscopic micrometeorite impacts.

facts.text: Colossal squids possess eyes measuring eleven inches across—comparable to large dinner plates—to spot bioluminescent sperm whales in pitch-black abyssal waters.
facts.claimText: The colossal squid has the largest documented eyes in the animal kingdom.
facts.explanation: These massive lenses maximize photon gathering in deep zones where sunlight never penetrates.

facts.text: Deep sea hydrothermal vents spew mineral-rich water heated past four hundred degrees Celsius, yet water remains liquid due to crushing hydrostatic pressure.
facts.claimText: Deep-sea hydrothermal vents heat water past 400 degrees Celsius, yet it stays liquid because of immense ocean-floor pressure.
facts.explanation: At abyssal depths, extreme hydrostatic pressure prevents superheated vent water from boiling into steam.

facts.text: More historical artifacts and shipwrecks lie submerged beneath the ocean surface than in all the terrestrial museums on Earth combined.
facts.claimText: More historical artifacts lie submerged on the ocean floor than are housed in all the museums on Earth combined.
facts.explanation: Thousands of years of maritime trade and shipwrecks have left an estimated three million vessels preserved across the seabed.

facts.text: The immortal jellyfish Turritopsis dohrnii can actively revert its adult cells back into juvenile polyp colonies when injured or facing starvation.
facts.claimText: The immortal jellyfish Turritopsis dohrnii can revert its adult cells back into a juvenile polyp state when stressed or injured.
facts.explanation: Through cellular transdifferentiation, adult medusa cells transform back into immature polyp colonies, bypassing normal aging.

facts.text: Underwater waterfalls exist beneath ocean straits, including the Denmark Strait cataract where cold water plunges over eleven thousand feet.
facts.claimText: The world's tallest waterfall is actually underwater in the Denmark Strait, where dense cold water plunges over 11,000 feet.
facts.explanation: Cold, dense Nordic Sea water sinks beneath warmer Irminger Sea water, creating a colossal submarine cataract.

facts.text: Ancient Roman concrete grew stronger over decades when exposed to seawater because volcanic ash and lime formed rare crystals that self-healed microcracks.
facts.claimText: Ancient Roman seawater concrete crumbled within decades because volcanic ash reacted destructively with Mediterranean salt.
facts.explanation: Myth! Seawater percolating through Roman volcanic ash and lime actually grew interlocking aluminous tobermorite crystals that strengthened the concrete.

facts.text: The ancient Library of Alexandria was not destroyed in a single catastrophic inferno, but slowly declined through neglect, civil warfare, and funding cuts over centuries.
facts.claimText: The Library of Alexandria was completely erased in a single overnight fire rather than declining over several centuries.
facts.explanation: Myth! Historical records show the Library suffered gradual decline across centuries due to funding cuts, civil conflicts, and political instability.

facts.text: Gladiators in ancient Rome ate a predominantly vegetarian diet rich in barley, beans, and ash tonics to build a thick subcutaneous fat layer for blade protection.
facts.claimText: Roman gladiators consumed vast quantities of red meat before matches.
facts.explanation: Historical bone isotope analyses revealed gladiators were nicknamed 'barley-men' and consumed plant-based carbohydrates.

facts.text: Cleopatra lived chronologically closer to the invention of the iPhone and the Moon landing than to the initial construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
facts.claimText: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing and the iPhone than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
facts.explanation: The Great Pyramid was completed around 2560 BCE, nearly 2,500 years before Cleopatra, whereas modern technology arrived less than 2,000 years after her.

facts.text: Viking raiders used calcite crystals known as Icelandic spar to locate the hidden position of the Sun behind dense fog and snowstorms.
facts.claimText: Viking navigators used sunstones to detect polarized light through heavy overcast clouds.
facts.explanation: Birefringence in optical calcite crystals splits light rays, pinpointing celestial polarization patterns.

facts.text: Water can boil and freeze simultaneously at a precise combination of temperature and pressure known to physicists as the thermodynamic triple point.
facts.claimText: Water can boil and freeze at the exact same time when held at a specific pressure and temperature called the triple point.
facts.explanation: At 0.01 degrees Celsius and 611.657 pascals, solid ice, liquid water, and water vapor coexist in thermodynamic equilibrium.

facts.text: Glass is not an ultra-slow flowing liquid; centuries-old cathedral windows are thicker at the bottom solely because medieval glassblowers mounted uneven panes that way.
facts.claimText: Medieval cathedral windows are thicker at the bottom because glass is a slow-flowing liquid that sags over centuries.
facts.explanation: Myth! Glass is an amorphous solid; old panes are uneven because medieval glassmakers spun crown glass of varying thickness and mounted the heavy edge down.

facts.text: Bananas produce a tiny detectable pulse of antimatter approximately every seventy-five minutes because they contain potassium-40 which undergoes positron decay.
facts.claimText: An ordinary banana emits a tiny pulse of antimatter roughly every 75 minutes due to naturally occurring potassium-40.
facts.explanation: Trace potassium-40 isotopes in bananas occasionally undergo beta-plus decay, releasing a positron (the antimatter counterpart of an electron).

facts.text: Hot water can freeze faster than cold water under specific thermal and evaporation conditions, a puzzling thermodynamic quirk termed the Mpemba effect.
facts.claimText: Under certain conditions, hot water can freeze faster than cold water—a phenomenon known as the Mpemba effect.
facts.explanation: Evaporation, convection currents, and dissolved gas differences can allow warmer water to reach freezing before an identical volume of cooler water.

facts.text: If two identical smooth pieces of the same metal touch in the vacuum of outer space, they permanently fuse together in an instantaneous process called cold welding.
facts.claimText: Two smooth pieces of the same bare metal touching in the vacuum of space will permanently fuse together via cold welding.
facts.explanation: Without atmospheric oxygen to form a protective oxide barrier on metal surfaces, metallic atoms share electrons on contact and bond into one piece.

facts.text: Wombats produce distinctive cube-shaped droppings to prevent their territory markers from rolling away off rocks and elevated mounds.
facts.claimText: Wombats have cubic feces produced by variable intestine wall elasticity.
facts.explanation: Stiff and flexible intestinal grooves shape the feces into six-sided prisms during the final eight percent of digestion.

facts.text: Hummingbirds are the only known birds capable of sustained backward flight and upside-down maneuvers thanks to specialized ball-and-socket shoulder joints.
facts.claimText: Swallows and swifts are the only birds capable of sustained backward flight alongside hummingbirds.
facts.explanation: Myth! Hummingbirds are the only known birds capable of sustained backward flight thanks to their unique rotary ball-and-socket shoulder joints.

facts.text: Octopus arms possess autonomous neural clusters containing two-thirds of the creature's total neurons, allowing severed tentacles to taste and grip independently.
facts.claimText: Two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are located in its arms rather than its central brain, allowing the arms to taste and react independently.
facts.explanation: Each octopus arm contains an autonomous axial nerve cord packed with sensory and motor neurons.

facts.text: Trees in mature old-growth forests share carbohydrates and distress signals with vulnerable saplings across extensive subterranean fungal mycorrhizal networks.
facts.claimText: Forest trees exchange carbon nutrients and chemical warning signals with neighboring saplings through underground fungal networks.
facts.explanation: Subterranean mycorrhizal fungi connect tree roots symbiotically, transferring carbohydrates, nitrogen, and defense signals.

facts.text: Beavers have orange-tinted teeth because their enamel is fortified with dense iron compounds, providing the tensile strength to chew through hardwood trunks.
facts.claimText: Beavers have bright orange teeth because their diet of tree bark stains their calcium enamel over time.
facts.explanation: Myth! Beaver tooth enamel is naturally fortified with iron compounds, which gives their incisors an orange hue and mechanical strength to gnaw hardwood.

facts.text: The human brain generates about twenty watts of electrical energy while awake—sufficient power to illuminate a low-draw LED desk lamp.
facts.claimText: While awake, the human brain generates roughly 20 watts of electrical power—enough to run a dim LED desk light.
facts.explanation: Billions of firing cortical neurons consume about 20% of the body's energy while operating on roughly 20 watts of power.

facts.text: The persistent urban myth that humans use only ten percent of their brain is completely false; functional brain scans show nearly every brain region activates daily.
facts.claimText: Humans only use 10 percent of their brain capacity during normal daily life, leaving 90 percent dormant.
facts.explanation: Myth! Modern fMRI and PET neuroimaging confirm that virtually every region of the human brain is active across daily tasks and sleep.

facts.text: Your brain actively rewires and prunes synaptic connections during deep slow-wave sleep, effectively flushing out metabolic toxins through the glymphatic system.
facts.suggestedSourceName: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders
facts.confirmedSourceName: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders
facts.claimText: During deep slow-wave sleep, the brain flushes out metabolic waste products through its glymphatic fluid system.
facts.explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid flows through interstitial brain spaces during deep sleep, clearing proteins and metabolic byproducts.

facts.text: People experiencing the phantom vibration syndrome feel their smartphone buzzing in their pocket due to the brain misinterpreting subtle muscle twitches.
facts.claimText: Phantom phone vibrations happen because phone radiation alters skin receptors.
facts.explanation: It is a perceptual signal-detection error caused by habitual sensory anticipation, not cellular radiation.

facts.text: Synesthesia is a harmless neurological condition where sensory pathways cross, allowing certain people to hear colors, taste shapes, or see musical chords.
facts.claimText: Synesthesia is a neurological trait where stimulation of one sense automatically triggers another, such as seeing colors when hearing music.
facts.explanation: Cross-activation between adjacent sensory regions in the cortex causes synesthetes to experience merged sensory perceptions.

facts.text: The first computer mouse, crafted in 1964 by Douglas Engelbart, was carved out of solid pine wood and contained two perpendicular mechanical wheels.
facts.claimText: The very first computer mouse built in 1964 by Douglas Engelbart was crafted out of a hollow pine wood block with two metal wheels.
facts.explanation: Engelbart and Bill English built the prototype X-Y position indicator at Stanford Research Institute using a carved wooden shell.

facts.text: More than ninety-nine percent of intercontinental internet traffic travels across underwater fiber-optic submarine cables rather than satellites.
facts.claimText: Over 80 percent of international internet data is beamed through geostationary satellites rather than ocean cables.
facts.explanation: Myth! More than 99% of intercontinental data traffic travels through hundreds of thousands of miles of undersea fiber-optic cables.

facts.text: The Apollo Guidance Computer used to navigate astronauts to the Moon operated on just four kilobytes of RAM and sixty-four kilobytes of ROM.
facts.claimText: The Apollo Guidance Computer that landed astronauts on the Moon had only 4 kilobytes of RAM and 64 kilobytes of ROM.
facts.explanation: MIT engineers used hand-woven core rope memory and real-time priority scheduling to guide Apollo missions within tiny memory limits.

facts.text: The famous QWERTY keyboard layout was created to slow down fast typists so early mechanical typewriter keys would not collide and jam.
facts.claimText: QWERTY layout was designed to optimize typing speed above all other ergonomic factors.
facts.explanation: Christopher Sholes placed common letter pairs apart to prevent neighboring mechanical hammers from entangling.

facts.text: The sentence 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is a pangram because it contains every single letter in the English alphabet at least once.
facts.claimText: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is called a palindrome because it uses every letter of the English alphabet.
facts.explanation: Myth! A sentence containing every letter of the alphabet at least once is called a pangram, whereas a palindrome reads the same backward and forward.

facts.text: There are over two hundred indigenous languages still spoken across Papua New Guinea that have fewer than one thousand native speakers worldwide.
facts.claimText: Papua New Guinea is home to over 200 indigenous languages that each have fewer than 1,000 native speakers.
facts.explanation: With over 800 total languages across rugged mountain valleys, Papua New Guinea is the most linguistically diverse nation on Earth.

facts.text: The ampersand symbol '&' was once officially recognized as the twenty-seventh letter of the English alphabet in early nineteenth-century schools.
facts.claimText: The ampersand symbol '&' was once taught in 19th-century schools as the 27th letter of the English alphabet.
facts.explanation: Schoolchildren reciting the alphabet ended with 'X, Y, Z, and per se and', which slurred into the word 'ampersand'.

facts.text: Honey excavated by archaeologists from ancient Egyptian royal tombs remains chemically stable, perfectly preserved, and edible after over three millennia.
facts.claimText: Raw honey never spoils under proper sealed conditions due to low moisture and high acidity.
facts.explanation: High osmotic pressure, trace hydrogen peroxide, and a low pH around 3.5 suppress bacterial growth indefinitely.

facts.text: Wasabi served in most commercial restaurants worldwide is not real Wasabia japonica, but rather horseradish paste dyed green with food coloring.
facts.claimText: Most green wasabi served in restaurants outside Japan is actually dyed horseradish paste rather than true Wasabia japonica.
facts.explanation: True Wasabia japonica rhizomes are difficult to cultivate and lose flavor within minutes of grating, so most restaurants use horseradish and mustard.

facts.text: Nutmeg can cause visual hallucinations, dizziness, and intense nausea if consumed in high quantities because it contains the psychoactive compound myristicin.
facts.claimText: Consuming large amounts of nutmeg is completely harmless because it contains no psychoactive compounds.
facts.explanation: Myth! Nutmeg contains myristicin, a compound that in high doses can induce severe nausea, dizziness, and hallucinations.

facts.text: Apples, pears, peaches, cherries, strawberries, and almonds all belong to the exact same botanical family of plants: the Rosaceae rose family.
facts.claimText: Apples, peaches, cherries, strawberries, and almonds all belong to the rose family (Rosaceae).
facts.explanation: Many orchard fruits and almonds share the five-petaled floral structure and genetics of the botanical family Rosaceae.

facts.text: Pure white chocolate contains zero cocoa solids or cocoa liquor, consisting only of cocoa butter fat, milk powder, sugar, and vanilla aromatics.
facts.claimText: White chocolate contains dark cocoa solids bleached white through alkaline processing.
facts.explanation: Myth! White chocolate contains zero cocoa solids; it is made exclusively from pale cocoa butter fat, milk solids, sugar, and vanilla.

facts.text: The Antarctic Ice Sheet contains nearly seventy percent of all the accessible freshwater on planet Earth and ninety percent of our total glacial ice.
facts.claimText: The Antarctic Ice Sheet holds roughly 70 percent of Earth's freshwater and 90 percent of its glacial ice.
facts.explanation: Locked in ice up to nearly three miles thick, Antarctica stores the vast majority of the planet's surface freshwater.

facts.text: Catatumbo lightning in Venezuela strikes Lake Maracaibo up to two hundred and sixty nights each year, producing thousands of lightning bolts every single hour.
facts.claimText: Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela experiences Catatumbo lightning storms up to 260 nights a year, generating thousands of flashes per hour.
facts.explanation: Warm Caribbean winds colliding with cold Andean mountain air over Lake Maracaibo create Earth's highest concentration of lightning.

facts.text: A standard cumulus cloud drifting overhead on a pleasant sunny afternoon weighs around five hundred thousand kilograms, or over one million pounds.
facts.claimText: A typical fluffy white cumulus cloud floating in a summer sky weighs less than a compact car.
facts.explanation: Myth! An average one-cubic-kilometer cumulus cloud contains droplets totaling roughly 500,000 kilograms (over 1.1 million pounds).

facts.text: Earth is not a perfect sphere; centrifugal force caused by planetary rotation causes the equator to bulge, making the summit of Mount Chimborazo closest to space.
facts.claimText: Because Earth bulges at the equator, the summit of Ecuador's Mount Chimborazo is farther from Earth's center than Mount Everest.
facts.explanation: Equatorial centrifugal bulge places Chimborazo's peak about 2 kilometers farther from Earth's core than Everest, despite lower elevation above sea level.

facts.text: The smell of fresh rain falling on dry soil after a long drought is termed petrichor, caused by plant oils and bacterial geosmin aerosolized by raindrops.
facts.claimText: The earthy scent of rain falling on dry ground is called petrichor, produced by plant oils and soil bacteria compounds.
facts.explanation: Falling raindrops trap tiny air bubbles that burst upward, releasing aerosols of plant oils and actinobacteria geosmin into the breeze.

facts.text: The name of the tallest known volcano and mountain in the Solar System, located on Mars is Olympus Mons.
facts.claimText: The name of the tallest known volcano and mountain in the Solar System, located on Mars is Olympus Mons.
facts.explanation: Olympus Mons is a shield volcano on Mars standing roughly 21.9 km (13.6 miles) high, nearly three times the height of Mount Everest.

facts.text: Alpha Centauri is the closest star system known neighbor to our Solar System.
facts.claimText: Vega is the closest star system known neighbor to our Solar System.
facts.explanation: Myth! Alpha Centauri is the closest star system known neighbor to our Solar System. The Alpha Centauri triple-star system, specifically Proxima Centauri at about 4.24 light-years away, is the closest star system to the Sun.

facts.text: The largest moon in the Solar System, even larger in diameter than the planet Mercury is Ganymede.
facts.claimText: The largest moon in the Solar System, even larger in diameter than the planet Mercury is Ganymede.
facts.explanation: Orbiting Jupiter, Ganymede has a diameter of 5,268 km, making it larger than Mercury (4,879 km) and Pluto.

facts.text: Mercury is the only chemical element metal that is liquid at standard room temperature and pressure.
facts.claimText: Cesium is the only chemical element metal that is liquid at standard room temperature and pressure.
facts.explanation: Myth! Mercury is the only chemical element metal that is liquid at standard room temperature and pressure. Mercury melts at -38.83°C (-37.89°F). Bromine is also liquid at room temperature, but it is a halogen non-metal.

facts.text: Higgs boson is the subatomic particle that was predicted by Peter Higgs in 1964 and confirmed at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012.
facts.claimText: Higgs boson is the subatomic particle that was predicted by Peter Higgs in 1964 and confirmed at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012.
facts.explanation: The Higgs boson is the quantum excitation of the Higgs field, which gives mass to fundamental particles.

facts.text: Polonium is the radioactive element that was discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898 and named after Marie's homeland.
facts.claimText: Radium is the radioactive element that was discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898 and named after Marie's homeland.
facts.explanation: Myth! Polonium is the radioactive element that was discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898 and named after Marie's homeland. Polonium (atomic number 84) was named after Poland, where Marie Skłodowska-Curie was born.

facts.text: The hardest naturally occurring substance known on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness is Diamond.
facts.claimText: The hardest naturally occurring substance known on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness is Diamond.
facts.explanation: Diamond defines 10 on the Mohs hardness scale due to its rigid three-dimensional lattice of covalent carbon-carbon bonds.

facts.text: Nutmeg is the spice that was once so prized in medieval Europe and the Maluku Islands that the Dutch traded the island of Manhattan to the British in 1667 to secure a monopoly on it.
facts.claimText: Cardamom is the spice that was once so prized in medieval Europe and the Maluku Islands that the Dutch traded the island of Manhattan to the British in 1667 to secure a monopoly on it.
facts.explanation: Myth! Nutmeg is the spice that was once so prized in medieval Europe and the Maluku Islands that the Dutch traded the island of Manhattan to the British in 1667 to secure a monopoly on it. In the Treaty of Breda (1667), the Dutch ceded New Amsterdam (Manhattan) while keeping Run Island in the Banda archipelago for its nutmeg trees.

facts.text: The deepest known point in Earth's oceans, located in the western Pacific Ocean is Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench.
facts.claimText: The deepest known point in Earth's oceans, located in the western Pacific Ocean is Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench.
facts.explanation: Challenger Deep reaches a depth of roughly 10,935 meters (35,876 feet) below sea level.

facts.text: Platypus is the mammal that is one of the very few venomous mammals, with males possessing ankle spurs that deliver excruciating venom.
facts.claimText: Capuchin Monkey is the mammal that is one of the very few venomous mammals, with males possessing ankle spurs that deliver excruciating venom.
facts.explanation: Myth! Platypus is the mammal that is one of the very few venomous mammals, with males possessing ankle spurs that deliver excruciating venom. Male platypuses have hollow spurs on their hind legs connected to crural glands that produce venom during the breeding season.

facts.text: The largest living animal ever known to have existed on Earth, surpassing even the largest known dinosaurs in mass is Blue Whale.
facts.claimText: The largest living animal ever known to have existed on Earth, surpassing even the largest known dinosaurs in mass is Blue Whale.
facts.explanation: Reaching lengths of up to 30 meters (98 feet) and weights up to 190 metric tons, the blue whale's heart alone is the size of a small car.

facts.text: Turritopsis dohrnii (Immortal Jellyfish) is the jellyfish species that is biologically capable of reverting from its mature medusa stage back into an immature polyp stage when stressed.
facts.claimText: Portuguese Man o' War is the jellyfish species that is biologically capable of reverting from its mature medusa stage back into an immature polyp stage when stressed.
facts.explanation: Myth! Turritopsis dohrnii (Immortal Jellyfish) is the jellyfish species that is biologically capable of reverting from its mature medusa stage back into an immature polyp stage when stressed. Through cellular transdifferentiation, Turritopsis dohrnii can transform its adult cells back into a juvenile polyp colony.

facts.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the world's first published computer algorithm in 1843, designed for Charles Babbage's mechanical Analytical Engine.

facts.text: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system.
facts.claimText: Jupiter is the hottest planet in our solar system.
facts.explanation: Myth! Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system. Your gut says Mercury because it sits closest to the Sun. But Venus's thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat so aggressively that surface temperatures hit 470°C. Mercury, with no atmosphere, can't hold onto its heat at all.

facts.text: The most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere is Nitrogen.
facts.claimText: The most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere is Nitrogen.
facts.explanation: Oxygen gets all the attention because we breathe it. Nitrogen makes up over three-quarters of every breath you take and you never notice it.

facts.text: The smallest bone in the human body is the stapes.
facts.claimText: The smallest bone in the human body is the stapes.

facts.text: The chemical formula for table salt is NaCl.

facts.text: The speed of light in a vacuum is 299,792 km/s.
facts.claimText: The speed of light in a vacuum is 30,000 km/s.
facts.explanation: Myth! The speed of light in a vacuum is 299,792 km/s. Everyone knows 'the speed of light' as a concept. Ask for the actual number and watch the confidence evaporate. The round approximation is 300,000 km/s, but the precise figure is 299,792,458 m/s.

facts.text: The chemical symbol for potassium is K.
facts.claimText: The chemical symbol for potassium is K.
facts.explanation: From the Latin 'kalium,' via the Arabic 'al-qalyah' (plant ashes). English speakers expect 'P' or 'Po,' but P is phosphorus and Po is polonium.

facts.text: The largest desert in the world is Antarctica.
facts.claimText: The largest desert in the world is The Arabian Desert.
facts.explanation: Myth! The largest desert in the world is Antarctica. Nearly everyone says the Sahara. A desert is defined by precipitation, not temperature. Antarctica receives less than 200 mm of precipitation per year and covers 14 million km², making it almost twice the size of the Sahara.

facts.text: The capital of Australia is Canberra.
facts.claimText: The capital of Australia is Canberra.
facts.explanation: Sydney and Melbourne compete for everything in Australia, including the wrong answer to this question. Canberra was built as a compromise capital specifically because the two cities couldn't stop arguing.

facts.text: The deepest point in the ocean is Challenger Deep.
facts.claimText: The deepest point in the ocean is Puerto Rico Trench.
facts.explanation: Myth! The deepest point in the ocean is Challenger Deep. Deeper than Mount Everest is tall. Only four people have ever been to the bottom. The pressure down there is over 1,000 atmospheres.

facts.text: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world.
facts.claimText: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world.
facts.explanation: Contains roughly 20% of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater. That single lake holds more water than all five Great Lakes combined.

facts.text: The longest mountain range on land is the Andes.
facts.claimText: The longest mountain range on land is the Andes.
facts.explanation: Runs through seven South American countries. The Rockies get picked by North Americans, the Himalayas by everyone else. Neither comes close in length.

facts.text: The smallest country in the world by area is Vatican City.
facts.claimText: The smallest country in the world by area is Vatican City.
facts.explanation: Fits inside Rome's city limits. Monaco is the second smallest at 2.02 km², roughly five times larger. Some people confuse Monaco with Vatican City because both are European microstates.

facts.text: The Nile is the longest river in the world.
facts.claimText: The Congo is the longest river in the world.
facts.explanation: Myth! The Nile is the longest river in the world. The Amazon gives it a serious fight depending on which tributaries you measure. By most accepted measurements, the Nile still wins by a narrow margin.

facts.text: The driest inhabited continent is Australia.
facts.claimText: The driest inhabited continent is Australia.
facts.explanation: Antarctica is drier, but 'inhabited' does the heavy lifting in this question. Australia's interior is vast desert, and even the populated coasts are surprisingly arid compared to other continents.

facts.text: The only continent with no active volcanoes is Australia.
facts.claimText: The only continent with no active volcanoes is Europe.
facts.explanation: Myth! The only continent with no active volcanoes is Australia. Sits in the middle of a tectonic plate rather than at its edges. No plate boundaries, no volcanic activity. The last eruption on the Australian mainland was over 5,000 years ago at Mount Gambier.

facts.text: Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
facts.claimText: Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
facts.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci is the reflex answer for any Renaissance art question. Michelangelo spent four years on his back painting it. He considered himself a sculptor first and resented the commission.

facts.text: The Mongol Empire is the empire that was ruled by Genghis Khan.
facts.claimText: The Roman Empire is the empire that was ruled by Genghis Khan.
facts.explanation: Myth! The Mongol Empire is the empire that was ruled by Genghis Khan. At its peak, the largest contiguous land empire in history. Stretched from Korea to Hungary. People sometimes guess the Ottoman or Persian Empire because those names feel bigger.

facts.text: The shortest war in history was the Anglo-Zanzibar War.
facts.claimText: The shortest war in history was the Anglo-Zanzibar War.
facts.explanation: Britain issued an ultimatum. Zanzibar didn't comply. The Royal Navy opened fire. Forty-five minutes later it was over. Barely long enough for a lunch break.

facts.text: The name of the ship the Pilgrims sailed to America in 1620 was the Mayflower.
facts.claimText: The name of the ship the Pilgrims sailed to America in 1620 was the Mayflower.
facts.explanation: Straightforward for Americans. Catches international players off guard. The voyage took 66 days and carried 102 passengers.

facts.text: Martin Luther King Jr wrote the 'I Have a Dream' speech.
facts.claimText: Martin Luther King Jr wrote the 'I Have a Dream' speech.
facts.explanation: The 'dream' section was partially improvised. King departed from his prepared text, prompted by gospel singer Mahalia Jackson calling out 'Tell them about the dream, Martin!'

facts.text: The largest organ in the human body is the skin.
facts.claimText: The largest organ in the human body is the skin.
facts.explanation: People reach for the liver or lungs. The skin covers about 1.7 square meters on an average adult and weighs around 3.6 kg. Hard to see it as an 'organ' when you're wearing it.

facts.text: The most spoken language in the world by native speakers is Mandarin Chinese.
facts.claimText: The most spoken language in the world by native speakers is Mandarin Chinese.
facts.explanation: English dominates as a second language, which is why it feels like the right answer. By native speakers alone, Mandarin leads with over 900 million.

facts.text: The smallest prime number is 2.
facts.claimText: The smallest prime number is 1.
facts.explanation: Myth! The smallest prime number is 2. And the only even prime. People say 1, but 1 is not prime by mathematical convention. A prime must have exactly two distinct factors: 1 and itself. The number 1 has only one factor.

facts.text: Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone.
facts.claimText: Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone.
facts.explanation: Antonio Meucci filed a caveat for a similar device five years earlier but couldn't afford the patent renewal fee. Elisha Gray filed his patent application the same day as Bell. The history is messier than the textbook version.

facts.text: The tallest building in the world is Burj Khalifa.
facts.claimText: The tallest building in the world is Shanghai Tower.
facts.explanation: Myth! The tallest building in the world is Burj Khalifa. Completed in 2010 and still unbeaten in 2026. The Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia was designed to surpass it but has faced construction delays for years.

facts.text: The national sport of Japan is Sumo wrestling.
facts.claimText: The national sport of Japan is Sumo wrestling.
facts.explanation: Baseball is wildly popular in Japan, which is why it gets picked. But sumo holds the official title of national sport, rooted in Shinto ritual and centuries of tradition.

facts.text: The main ingredient in hummus is Chickpeas.
facts.claimText: The main ingredient in hummus is Soybeans.
facts.explanation: Myth! The main ingredient in hummus is Chickpeas. The word 'hummus' literally means 'chickpeas' in Arabic. Tahini is the second key ingredient, but chickpeas do the heavy lifting.

facts.text: The most consumed beverage in the world after water is Tea.
facts.claimText: The most consumed beverage in the world after water is Tea.
facts.explanation: Coffee drinkers are absolutely certain it's coffee. Tea wins by volume across China, India, and the rest of Asia. Coffee dominates the West but can't match tea's global reach.

facts.text: The primary ingredient in tofu is Soybeans.
facts.claimText: The primary ingredient in tofu is Rice.
facts.explanation: Myth! The primary ingredient in tofu is Soybeans. Soy milk is coagulated and pressed into blocks. The process is similar to cheese-making. Rice gets guessed often, probably because tofu appears alongside rice so frequently.

facts.text: The name of Thor's hammer in Norse mythology is Mjölnir.
facts.claimText: The name of Thor's hammer in Norse mythology is Mjölnir.
facts.explanation: Pronounced roughly 'MYOL-nir.' Marvel movies made the name famous, but spelling it correctly still trips up most people.

facts.text: Loki is the Norse god of mischief.
facts.claimText: Baldur is the Norse god of mischief.
facts.explanation: Myth! Loki is the Norse god of mischief. Not actually a god in the traditional sense. Loki is a jötunn (giant) who lives among the Aesir gods. The Marvel version made him Thor's brother; the original myths make their relationship much more complicated.

facts.text: The name of the underworld river of forgetfulness in Greek mythology is the River Lethe.
facts.claimText: The name of the underworld river of forgetfulness in Greek mythology is the River Lethe.
facts.explanation: Drinking from Lethe erased all memories. Dead souls drank before reincarnation. The Styx gets picked because it's more famous, but the Styx is the river of hatred, not forgetfulness.

facts.text: Mars was the Roman god of war.
facts.claimText: Neptune was the Roman god of war.
facts.explanation: Myth! Mars was the Roman god of war. The Greek equivalent is Ares. Mars was far more respected in Roman culture than Ares was in Greek mythology. The Romans named a planet, a month (March), and a field (Campus Martius) after him.

facts.text: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom.
facts.claimText: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom.
facts.explanation: Also the goddess of warfare and crafts. She sprang fully armored from Zeus's forehead after he swallowed her pregnant mother Metis. Athens is named after her.

facts.explanation: Myth! The name of the fictional continent in Game of Thrones is Westeros. Essos is the eastern continent where Daenerys spends most of her time. People mix them up because the show bounces between both constantly.

facts.explanation: Everyone says 'Alfred.' Few remember the surname. Pennyworth has been Batman's moral compass since 1943.
